description: Replaces the amplitude envelope of input 1 with the envelope extracted from input 2: the target's own envelope is flattened out first, then the donor's contour is applied - contrast envel impose, which multiplies the donor's envelope on top of the target's. Pinned to mode 1 (donor is a soundfile; SoundThread's envel_replace_1); modes 2-4 take binary .env / text breakpoint envelopes and are not curated. Output duration equals input 1's duration exactly (sample-exact on all probes). Verified with the repo's analysis.trajectory_frames: replacing the envelope of an undulating noise source with a 4-pulse donor gives an output RMS trajectory correlating with the donor at r = 0.96 (the unprocessed target correlated at 0.03), and the result audibly differs from envel impose on the same pair (outputs not byte-identical). Mono and stereo targets both work.
musical_use: Envelope transplant rather than envelope combination: the target's dynamics are erased and the donor's are written in. The canonical CDP use (quoted in the manual) is restoring a sound's original contour after a process that mangled levels - e.g. filtering with time-varying Q - by using the pre-process sound as the donor. Musically it is the stronger form of the offline sidechain: where impose leaves the target's internal dynamics ghosting through, replace makes the target follow the donor's rhythm with full commitment - drum-machine-tight gating of pads, speech rhythm stamped onto texture. Beware targets with near-silent passages: flattening cannot meaningfully rescale what is almost zero (manual caveat), so noise floors get boosted - choose sustained, healthy-level targets.

wsize.description: Envelope-scanning window in milliseconds, used for both the flattening of input 1 and the sampling of input 2. CDP-enforced range 5 to input 1's duration in ms (input-dependent, same rule verified on envel impose). SoundThread default 20. Breakpoint file refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').

examples.description: Transplant a percussive donor's rhythm onto sustained material, erasing its own swells.
examples.expected_use: inputs = [sustained target, rhythmic donor]; output follows only the donor's contour.

examples.description: Restore the original dynamic contour after a level-mangling process.
examples.expected_use: inputs = [processed sound, original sound]; the processed timbre gets its old dynamics back.

known_issues: Input order matters: input 1 is flattened and reshaped, input 2 is the envelope donor. Output duration = input 1's duration exactly (verified with donor shorter than target).
Near-zero amplitudes in the target cannot be meaningfully rescaled by the flattening stage (manual caveat) - low-level noise gets amplified; prefer healthy-level targets.
wsize's maximum is input 1's duration in ms (runtime-enforced, input-dependent; manual/afta8 attribute the bound to the donor - same documentation error as envel impose).
wsize rejects breakpoint files ('ERROR: Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.').
Deterministic: two runs 1.1 s apart produce identical decoded samples.
Verified distinct from envel impose on the same input pair (byte-level difference), with the replace output tracking the donor even where the target's own envelope disagreed.
